verses.modern: After Paul had seen the vision, we immediately sought to go to Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

verses.kjv: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
verses.modern: Setting sail from Troas, we went straight to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis.

verses.kjv: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
verses.modern: From there we went to Philippi, which is a leading city of that part of Macedonia and a Roman colony. We stayed in that city for some days.

verses.kjv: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.
verses.modern: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a riverside, where we supposed there was a place of prayer. We sat down and spoke to the women who had gathered there.

verses.kjv: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
verses.modern: A woman named Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who worshipped God, was listening. The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to what Paul was saying.

verses.kjv: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us.
verses.modern: When she and her household were baptized, she urged us, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay." She persuaded us to come.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:
verses.modern: As we were going to the place of prayer, a slave girl met us who had a spirit of divination. She brought her masters great profit by fortune-telling.

verses.kjv: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.
verses.modern: She followed Paul and the rest of us and cried out, "These men are servants of the Most High God, Who are telling You the way of salvation."

verses.kjv: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
verses.modern: She kept doing this for many days. Paul became greatly troubled. He turned and said to the spirit, "I command You in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her." It came out that very hour.

verses.kjv: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,
verses.modern: When her masters saw that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the authorities.

verses.kjv: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
verses.modern: They brought them before the magistrates, saying, "These men are Jews and are greatly disturbing our city.

verses.kjv: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
verses.modern: They are teaching customs that are not lawful for us to accept or practice, since we are Romans."

verses.kjv: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.
verses.modern: The crowd joined in the attack against them. The magistrates tore the clothes off Paul and Silas and ordered them to be beaten with rods.

verses.kjv: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
verses.modern: After inflicting many blows on them, they threw them into prison, ordering the jailer to keep them securely.

verses.kjv: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
verses.modern: Receiving this order, he put them in the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.

verses.kjv: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
verses.modern: Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

verses.kjv: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
verses.modern: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. All the doors immediately flew open, and everyone's chains were loosened.

verses.kjv: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
verses.modern: The jailer woke up and saw the prison doors standing open. He drew his sword and was about to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had escaped.

verses.kjv: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
verses.modern: But Paul called out loudly, "Do not harm yourself — we are all here!"

verses.kjv: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
verses.modern: The jailer called for lights and rushed in. Trembling, he fell down before Paul and Silas.

verses.kjv: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
verses.modern: He brought them outside and said, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"

verses.kjv: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
verses.modern: They said, "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and You will be saved — you and Your household."

verses.kjv: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
verses.modern: They spoke the word of the Lord to Him and to all who were in His house.

verses.kjv: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
verses.modern: He took them that same hour of the night and washed their wounds. He and His entire household were baptized right away.

verses.kjv: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
verses.modern: He brought them into His house and set food before them. He rejoiced greatly, having believed in God with His entire household.

verses.kjv: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
verses.modern: When day came, the magistrates sent officers with the order, "Release those men."

verses.kjv: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
verses.modern: The jailer reported these words to Paul: "The magistrates have sent word to release you. Go now and leave in peace."

verses.kjv: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
verses.modern: But Paul said to the officers, "They beat us publicly without a trial — and we are Roman citizens! They threw us into prison, and now they want to send us away secretly? No. Let them come themselves and lead us out."

verses.kjv: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
verses.modern: The officers reported this to the magistrates. When they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they were alarmed.

verses.kjv: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
verses.modern: They came and apologized to them. They led them out and asked them to leave the city.

verses.kjv: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
verses.modern: Paul and Silas left the prison and went to Lydia's house. They saw the brothers, encouraged them, and then departed.

chapters.summary: Paul chose Timothy as a companion, and the Spirit directed them to Macedonia where Lydia believed and was baptized at Philippi. Paul cast a spirit of divination out of a slave girl, was beaten and imprisoned with Silas, and at midnight an earthquake opened the prison doors. The jailer and his household believed and were baptized that night.

verses.kjv: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
verses.modern: Passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.

verses.kjv: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
verses.modern: As was his custom, Paul went in to them and for three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

verses.kjv: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.
verses.modern: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. "This Jesus, whom I am proclaiming to You, is the Christ," He said.

verses.kjv: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
verses.modern: Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a great number of devout Greeks and a good many leading women.

verses.kjv: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
verses.modern: But the unbelieving Jews were filled with jealousy. They recruited some wicked men from the marketplace, gathered a mob, and threw the city into an uproar. They attacked the house of Jason, looking for Paul and Silas to bring them before the crowd.

verses.kjv: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
verses.modern: When they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some of the brothers before the city rulers, shouting, "These men who have turned the world upside down have come here too!

verses.kjv: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
verses.modern: Jason has welcomed them. They all act against the decrees of Caesar, saying there is another king — Jesus."

verses.kjv: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
verses.modern: These things stirred up the crowd and the city rulers who heard them.

verses.kjv: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
verses.modern: They made Jason and the others post bond, and then released them.

verses.kjv: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.modern: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea. When they arrived, they went into the synagogue of the Jews.

verses.kjv: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
verses.modern: The people of Berea were more honorable than those in Thessalonica. They received the word with great eagerness and searched the Scriptures every day to see if these things were true.

verses.kjv: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
verses.modern: Many of them believed, as did a good number of prominent Greek women and men.

verses.kjv: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
verses.modern: When the Jews of Thessalonica learned that Paul was proclaiming the word of God at Berea, they came there too and stirred up the crowds.

verses.kjv: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
verses.modern: The brothers immediately sent Paul away to the coast, while Silas and Timothy remained behind.

verses.kjv: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
verses.modern: Those escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens. They left with instructions for Silas and Timothy to come to him as soon as possible.

verses.kjv: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
verses.modern: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply troubled to see how full of idols the city was.

verses.kjv: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
verses.modern: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and with the devout people, and in the marketplace every day with those he met.

verses.kjv: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
verses.modern: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also debated with Him. Some said, "What is this chatterbox trying to say?" Others said, "He seems to be proclaiming foreign gods" — because He was preaching Jesus and the resurrection.

verses.kjv: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
verses.modern: They took hold of Him and brought Him to the Areopagus. They said, "May we know what this new teaching is that You are presenting?

verses.kjv: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
verses.modern: Some of the things You say sound strange to us. We want to know what they mean."

verses.kjv: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
verses.modern: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing but talking about and listening to the latest ideas.

verses.kjv: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
verses.modern: Paul stood in the middle of Mars' hill and said, "Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are too superstitious.

verses.kjv: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
verses.modern: As I walked around and looked carefully at the things You worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. It is this very God — whom You worship without knowing — that I am declaring to You.

verses.kjv: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
verses.modern: God, Who made the world and everything in it, is Lord of heaven and earth. He does not live in temples made by human hands.

verses.kjv: Neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
verses.modern: He is not served by human hands as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives life and breath and everything to everyone.

verses.kjv: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
verses.modern: From one blood He made every nation of mankind to live on all the face of the earth. He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.

verses.kjv: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
verses.modern: He did this so that people would seek God and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him — though He is not far from each one of us.

verses.kjv: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
verses.modern: For in Him we live and move and have our being. As some of Your own poets have said, 'We are His offspring.'

verses.kjv: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device.
verses.modern: Since we are God's offspring, we should not think that the Godhead is like gold or silver or stone — shaped by human skill and imagination.

verses.kjv: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
verses.modern: In the past God overlooked such times of ignorance. But now He commands all people everywhere to repent.

verses.kjv: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
verses.modern: He has set a day on which He will judge the world in righteousness by the Man he has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead."

verses.kjv: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.
verses.modern: When they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked. Others said, "We will hear you again about this."

verses.kjv: So Paul departed from among them.
verses.modern: So Paul left from among them.

verses.kjv: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
verses.modern: But some men joined him and believed. Among them were Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

chapters.summary: Paul preached in Thessalonica where some Jews and many Greeks believed, but the unbelieving Jews stirred up a mob. The brethren sent Paul and Silas to Berea where the people searched the scriptures daily, and Paul went on to Athens where he preached on Mars' hill, declaring the unknown God and the resurrection of Christ.

verses.kjv: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
verses.modern: After these things Paul left Athens and came to Corinth.

verses.kjv: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
verses.modern: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them.

verses.kjv: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
verses.modern: Since he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and they worked together — for they were tentmakers by trade.

verses.kjv: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
verses.modern: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath and persuaded both Jews and Greeks.

verses.kjv: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
verses.modern: When Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself entirely to the word. He testified to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.

verses.kjv: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
verses.modern: When they resisted and insulted Him, He shook out His clothes and said to them, "Your blood is on Your own heads. I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."

verses.kjv: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man's house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
verses.modern: He left from there and went to the house of a man named Justus, a worshipper of God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.

verses.kjv: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
verses.modern: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord together with His entire household. Many of the Corinthians who heard also believed and were baptized.

verses.kjv: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
verses.modern: The Lord spoke to Paul one night in a vision: "Do not be afraid. Keep speaking — do not be silent.

verses.kjv: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
verses.modern: For I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you. I have many people in this city."

verses.kjv: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
verses.modern: Paul stayed there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

verses.kjv: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
verses.modern: When Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews made a united attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

verses.kjv: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
verses.modern: They said, "This man is persuading people to worship God in ways contrary to the law."

verses.kjv: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
verses.modern: Just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio said to the Jews, "If this were a matter of wrongdoing or serious crime, I would have reason to hear your complaint.

verses.kjv: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.
verses.modern: But since it is a question about words and names and your own law, see to it yourselves. I am not willing to be a judge of such matters."

verses.kjv: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
verses.modern: He drove them away from the judgment seat.

verses.kjv: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
verses.modern: Then all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But Gallio paid no attention to any of it.

verses.kjv: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
verses.modern: Paul stayed on for many more days. Then he said farewell to the brothers and sailed for Syria, with Priscilla and Aquila. He had his head shaved at Cenchrea because he had made a vow.

verses.kjv: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
verses.modern: They came to Ephesus, where he left Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

verses.kjv: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
verses.modern: When they asked him to stay longer, he declined.

verses.kjv: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
verses.modern: He said farewell to them, saying, "I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return to you again if God wills." Then He sailed from Ephesus.

verses.kjv: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
verses.modern: When he landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church, then went down to Antioch.

verses.kjv: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.modern: After spending some time there, he left and traveled through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

verses.kjv: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
verses.modern: A Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well-versed in the Scriptures.

verses.kjv: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
verses.modern: He had been taught the way of the Lord. He spoke with great enthusiasm and taught accurately the things about Jesus, though He knew only the baptism of John.

verses.kjv: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
verses.modern: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to Him the way of God more accurately.

verses.kjv: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
verses.modern: When Apollos wanted to cross to Achaia, the brothers encouraged Him and wrote to the disciples to welcome Him. When He arrived, He greatly helped those who through grace had believed.

verses.kjv: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
verses.modern: He powerfully refuted the Jews in public, demonstrating through the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

chapters.summary: Paul came to Corinth, lived with Aquila and Priscilla, and worked as a tentmaker while preaching in the synagogue every sabbath. The Lord told Paul in a vision not to be afraid, and he stayed a year and six months teaching the word. Apollos, an eloquent Alexandrian Jew, began preaching in Ephesus and was instructed more perfectly by Aquila and Priscilla.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts, came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
verses.modern: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul traveled through the upper regions and came to Ephesus. He found some disciples there

verses.kjv: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
verses.modern: and asked them, "Did You receive the Holy Ghost when You believed?" They replied, "We have not even heard that there is a Holy Ghost."

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism.
verses.modern: He said, "Then what baptism did You receive?" They said, "John's baptism."

verses.kjv: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
verses.modern: Paul said, "John baptized with a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him — that is, in Christ Jesus."

verses.kjv: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.modern: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.kjv: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
verses.modern: When Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Ghost came on them. They spoke with tongues and prophesied.

verses.kjv: And all the men were about twelve.
verses.modern: There were about twelve men in all.

verses.kjv: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.modern: He went into the synagogue and spoke boldly for three months, arguing and persuading them about the kingdom of God.

verses.kjv: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
verses.modern: But when some became stubborn and refused to believe — speaking evil of the Way before the crowd — Paul left them. He took the disciples with him and reasoned daily in the school of Tyrannus.

verses.kjv: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.modern: This went on for two years, so that all who lived in Asia — both Jews and Greeks — heard the word of the Lord Jesus.

verses.kjv: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
verses.modern: God did extraordinary miracles through Paul's hands.

verses.kjv: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
verses.modern: Even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were brought to the sick, and their diseases left them and the evil spirits came out of them.

verses.kjv: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
verses.modern: Some itinerant Jewish exorcists also tried invoking the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits. They would say, "I command You by the Jesus whom Paul preaches."

verses.kjv: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
verses.modern: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

verses.kjv: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
verses.modern: The evil spirit answered them, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know — but who are you?"

verses.kjv: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
verses.modern: The man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered all of them. He attacked with such force that they fled from the house naked and wounded.

verses.kjv: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
verses.modern: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus. Fear came over all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.

verses.kjv: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
verses.modern: Many who had believed came and openly confessed what they had done.

verses.kjv: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
verses.modern: Many who had practiced sorcery brought their scrolls together and burned them publicly. When they counted up the value, it came to fifty thousand pieces of silver.

verses.kjv: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
verses.modern: In this way the word of God grew mightily and spread.

verses.kjv: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
verses.modern: After these things were completed, Paul resolved in the Spirit to travel through Macedonia and Achaia and then go to Jerusalem. He said, "After I have been there, I must also see Rome."

verses.kjv: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
verses.modern: He sent two of his helpers — Timothy and Erastus — to Macedonia, while he himself stayed in Asia for a while.

verses.kjv: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
verses.modern: About that time there arose a serious disturbance about the Way.

verses.kjv: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
verses.modern: A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Diana, provided a great deal of business for the craftsmen.

verses.kjv: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
verses.modern: He called them together, along with the workers in similar trades, and said, "Men, you know that our prosperity comes from this business.

verses.kjv: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
verses.modern: You see and hear that this Paul has persuaded and turned away a great many people — not only in Ephesus but almost throughout all Asia. He says that gods made by human hands are not real gods.

verses.kjv: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
verses.modern: Our trade is in danger of falling into disrepute. Not only that, but the temple of the great goddess Diana may be discredited and her greatness destroyed — she whom all Asia and the world worship."

verses.kjv: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
verses.modern: When they heard this, they were filled with rage and began shouting, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"

verses.kjv: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
verses.modern: The city was filled with confusion. They seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul's traveling companions, and rushed together into the theater.

verses.kjv: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
verses.modern: Paul wanted to go in to the crowd, but the disciples would not let him.

verses.kjv: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
verses.modern: Even some of the leading officials of Asia who were his friends sent word urging him not to venture into the theater.

verses.kjv: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
verses.modern: Some shouted one thing and some another. The assembly was in confusion. Most of the people did not even know why they had gathered.

verses.kjv: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
verses.modern: Some from the crowd pulled Alexander forward, the Jews having pushed him out front. Alexander motioned with his hand and wanted to make a defense to the crowd.

verses.kjv: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
verses.modern: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, they all shouted together for about two hours, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"

verses.kjv: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
verses.modern: The city clerk quieted the crowd and said, "Men of Ephesus, who does not know that the city of Ephesus is the guardian of the great goddess Diana and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?

verses.kjv: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
verses.modern: Since these things cannot be denied, you should be calm and do nothing rash.

verses.kjv: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
verses.modern: You have brought these men here who are neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.

verses.kjv: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
verses.modern: If Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them bring charges against each other there.

verses.kjv: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
verses.modern: If there is any other matter you want to raise, it shall be settled in the legal assembly.

verses.kjv: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
verses.modern: We are in danger of being charged with rioting because of what has happened today. There is no justification we can give for this commotion."

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
verses.modern: When he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.

chapters.summary: Paul arrived in Ephesus, laid hands on twelve disciples who received the Holy Ghost, and taught for two years so that all who dwelt in Asia heard the word. God worked special miracles through Paul, and the seven sons of Sceva were overpowered by an evil spirit. The silversmith Demetrius stirred up a riot because Paul's preaching threatened the worship of Diana.

verses.kjv: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
verses.modern: After the uproar ended, Paul sent for the disciples. After encouraging them, he said farewell and set out for Macedonia.

verses.kjv: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
verses.modern: He traveled through that region, encouraging the believers with many words. Then he came to Greece,

verses.kjv: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
verses.modern: where he stayed for three months. When the Jews plotted against him just as he was about to sail to Syria, he decided to return through Macedonia.

verses.kjv: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.modern: He was accompanied to Asia by Sopater of Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, as well as Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia.

verses.kjv: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
verses.modern: These men went ahead and waited for us at Troas.

verses.kjv: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
verses.modern: We sailed from Philippi after the Feast of Unleavened Bread and joined them at Troas in five days. We stayed there for seven days.

verses.kjv: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
verses.modern: On the first day of the week, the disciples gathered to break bread. Paul spoke to them since he planned to leave the next day. He continued speaking until midnight.

verses.kjv: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
verses.modern: There were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.

verses.kjv: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
verses.modern: A young man named Eutychus was sitting in the window and sank into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. Overcome by sleep, he fell from the third floor and was picked up dead.

verses.kjv: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
verses.modern: Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. He said, "Do not be alarmed — his life is in him."

verses.kjv: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
verses.modern: Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. He talked with them for a long time — until daybreak — then left.

verses.kjv: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
verses.modern: The people took the young man home alive and were greatly comforted.

verses.kjv: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
verses.modern: We went ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul on board. He had arranged this because he intended to travel there on foot.

verses.kjv: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
verses.modern: When he met us at Assos, we took him on board and went to Mitylene.

verses.kjv: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
verses.modern: Sailing from there, we came the next day opposite Chios. The day after, we arrived at Samos and waited at Trogyllium. The following day we reached Miletus.

verses.kjv: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
verses.modern: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so he would not have to spend time in Asia. He was hurrying to be in Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

verses.kjv: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
verses.modern: From Miletus he sent word to Ephesus and called for the elders of the church.

verses.kjv: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
verses.modern: When they came to him, he said to them, "You know how I lived among you the entire time from the first day I arrived in Asia.

verses.kjv: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
verses.modern: I served the Lord with great humility, with tears, and through trials that came from the plots of the Jews.

verses.kjv: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
verses.modern: I did not hold back anything that was helpful to you. I taught you publicly and from house to house.

verses.kjv: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.modern: I declared to both Jews and Greeks that they must turn to God in repentance and have faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
verses.modern: Now I am going to Jerusalem, compelled by the Spirit. I do not know what will happen to me there.

verses.kjv: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
verses.modern: Only I know that in every city the Holy Ghost warns me that chains and hardship await me.

verses.kjv: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
verses.modern: None of these things move me. I do not count my life of any value to myself, so long as I can finish the race and complete the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus — to testify to the gospel of the grace of God.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
verses.modern: Now I know that none of You among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God will see my face again.

verses.kjv: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
verses.modern: Therefore I declare to You this day that I am innocent of the blood of everyone.

verses.kjv: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
verses.modern: For I did not hold back from declaring to You the whole counsel of God.

verses.kjv: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
verses.modern: Pay careful attention to yourselves and to all the flock over which the Holy Ghost has made You overseers. Shepherd the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.

verses.kjv: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
verses.modern: I know that after I leave, fierce wolves will come in among You and will not spare the flock.

verses.kjv: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
verses.modern: Even from Your own group, men will arise speaking twisted things in order to draw disciples away after them.

verses.kjv: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
verses.modern: So stay alert. Remember that for three years I never stopped warning each one of you night and day with tears.

verses.kjv: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
verses.modern: Now I commit You to God and to the word of His grace. He is able to build You up and give You an inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

verses.kjv: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel.
verses.modern: I have not coveted anyone's silver or gold or clothing.

verses.kjv: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
verses.modern: You yourselves know that these hands have provided for my own needs and for those who were with me.

verses.kjv: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
verses.modern: In all things I have shown You that by working hard like this we must help the weak. We must remember the words of the Lord Jesus: "It is more blessed to give than to receive."

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
verses.modern: When He had finished speaking, He knelt down and prayed with all of them.

verses.kjv: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,
verses.modern: They all wept greatly, fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him.

verses.kjv: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
verses.modern: They grieved most of all over his words — that they would see his face no more. Then they walked with him to the ship.

chapters.summary: Paul traveled through Macedonia and Greece, and at Troas he preached until midnight when the young man Eutychus fell from a window and was taken up dead, but Paul embraced him and his life came back. Paul called the Ephesian elders to Miletus and warned them that grievous wolves would enter among them, commending them to God and to the word of His grace.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
verses.modern: After we had parted from them and set sail, we went straight to Cos. The next day we went to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

verses.kjv: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
verses.modern: We found a ship crossing to Phenicia, went aboard, and set sail.

verses.kjv: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
verses.modern: We came within sight of Cyprus, passed it on our left, and sailed on to Syria. We landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

verses.kjv: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: We found the disciples there and stayed seven days. Through the Spirit they urged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
verses.modern: When our time was up, we left and continued on our way. All the disciples, with their wives and children, escorted us outside the city. We knelt down on the beach and prayed.

verses.kjv: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
verses.modern: Then we said farewell to one another, we boarded the ship, and they went back home.

verses.kjv: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
verses.modern: We completed our voyage from Tyre and arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

verses.kjv: And the next day we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
verses.modern: The next day we left and came to Caesarea. We entered the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the seven, and stayed with him.

verses.kjv: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
verses.modern: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

verses.kjv: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
verses.modern: While we were staying there for several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judaea.

verses.kjv: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
verses.modern: Coming to us, he took Paul's belt, bound his own hands and feet with it, and said, "The Holy Ghost says this: 'The Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.'"

verses.kjv: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: When we heard this, both we and the local people begged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.modern: Paul answered, "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."

verses.kjv: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
verses.modern: When He could not be persuaded, we stopped urging Him and said, "The will of the Lord be done."

verses.kjv: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: After these days we packed our bags and went up to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
verses.modern: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us and brought us to the home of Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to stay.

verses.kjv: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
verses.modern: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us gladly.

verses.kjv: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
verses.modern: The next day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were present.

verses.kjv: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
verses.modern: After greeting them, Paul reported in detail what God had done among the Gentiles through His ministry.

verses.kjv: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
verses.modern: When they heard this, they praised the Lord. They said to Paul, "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.

verses.kjv: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
verses.modern: They have been told about you that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn away from Moses — telling them not to circumcise their children or walk according to the customs.

verses.kjv: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
verses.modern: What is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.

verses.kjv: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
verses.modern: Do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.

verses.kjv: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
verses.modern: Take them and purify yourself along with them and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that the reports about you are false — that you yourself also live in obedience to the law.

verses.kjv: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
verses.modern: As for the Gentiles who have believed, we have sent them a letter with our decision that they should abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality."

verses.kjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
verses.modern: Then Paul took the men, and the next day he purified himself with them and went into the temple. He announced the completion of the days of purification, when an offering would be made for each of them.

verses.kjv: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
verses.modern: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from Asia saw him in the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,

verses.kjv: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
verses.modern: crying out, "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, our law, and this place! He has also brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place."

verses.kjv: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
verses.modern: They had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with Paul and assumed Paul had brought him into the temple.

verses.kjv: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
verses.modern: The whole city was stirred up and the people came running together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and the doors were immediately shut.

verses.kjv: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
verses.modern: While they were trying to kill him, a report reached the commander of the Roman regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

verses.kjv: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
verses.modern: He immediately took soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

verses.kjv: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
verses.modern: The commander came up, arrested Paul, and ordered him to be chained with two chains. He then asked who he was and what he had done.

verses.kjv: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
verses.modern: Some in the crowd shouted one thing and some another. Since the commander could not find out the facts because of the uproar, he ordered Paul to be brought into the barracks.

verses.kjv: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
verses.modern: When Paul reached the steps, the soldiers had to carry him because of the violent pressure of the crowd.

verses.kjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
verses.modern: The crowd followed, shouting, "Away with him!"

verses.kjv: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
verses.modern: As Paul was about to be taken into the barracks, he said to the commander, "May I say something to you?" The commander replied, "Do you know Greek?"

verses.kjv: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
verses.modern: "Aren't you the Egyptian who stirred up a revolt some time ago and led four thousand assassins out into the wilderness?"

verses.kjv: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
verses.modern: Paul replied, "I am a Jew, a citizen of Tarsus in Cilicia — no insignificant city. Please let me speak to the people."

verses.kjv: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
verses.modern: The commander gave permission, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd with his hand. When silence fell, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,

chapters.summary: Paul sailed to Jerusalem despite warnings from the brethren that bonds and afflictions awaited him. He met with James and the elders and agreed to purify himself at the temple, but Jews from Asia stirred up the crowd against him. The Roman soldiers rescued Paul from the mob and allowed him to address the people.

verses.kjv: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.
verses.modern: "Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense I now make before you."

verses.kjv: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
verses.modern: When they heard him speak to them in the Hebrew language, they became even quieter. He said,

verses.kjv: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
verses.modern: "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel and trained thoroughly in the law of our fathers. I was just as zealous for God as all of you are today.

verses.kjv: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
verses.modern: I persecuted the followers of this Way to the death, binding and delivering both men and women to prison.

verses.kjv: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
verses.modern: The high priest and the whole council of elders can testify to this. I also received letters from them to the brothers in Damascus. I went there to arrest those people and bring them back to Jerusalem to be punished.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
verses.modern: As I was traveling and approaching Damascus, around noon a very bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.

verses.kjv: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
verses.modern: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'

verses.kjv: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
verses.modern: I answered, 'Who are You, Lord?' He said to me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom You are persecuting.'

verses.kjv: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
verses.modern: My companions saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the One speaking to me.

verses.kjv: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
verses.modern: I asked, 'What shall I do, Lord?' The Lord said to me, 'Get up and go into Damascus. There You will be told everything You are appointed to do.'

verses.kjv: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
verses.modern: Since I could not see because of the brightness of that light, I was led by the hand of those who were with me into Damascus.

verses.kjv: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,
verses.modern: A man named Ananias, a devout man according to the law who had a good reputation among all the Jews living there,

verses.kjv: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
verses.modern: came to me, stood beside me, and said, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight.' That very hour I was able to see him.

verses.kjv: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
verses.modern: He said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will and to see the Righteous One and to hear his voice.

verses.kjv: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
verses.modern: For you will be His witness to all people of what you have seen and heard.

verses.kjv: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
verses.modern: Now, why do you wait? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on His name.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
verses.modern: When I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance

verses.kjv: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
verses.modern: and saw the Lord saying to me, 'Hurry and leave Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.'

verses.kjv: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
verses.modern: I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You in every synagogue.

verses.kjv: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
verses.modern: And when the blood of Your martyr Stephen was shed, I myself was standing by, approving of his death, and keeping the clothes of those who were killing him.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
verses.modern: But He said to me, 'Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"

verses.kjv: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
verses.modern: The crowd listened to Paul until he said this. Then they raised their voices and shouted, "Away with such a man from the earth! He is not fit to live!"

verses.kjv: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
verses.modern: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and hurling dust into the air,

verses.kjv: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
verses.modern: the commander ordered Paul to be brought into the barracks. He directed that he be examined by flogging so he could find out why they were shouting against him like this.

verses.kjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
verses.modern: As they stretched him out for the flogging, Paul said to the centurion standing nearby, "Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen who has not been condemned?"

verses.kjv: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
verses.modern: When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and said, "Be careful what you do. This man is a Roman citizen."

verses.kjv: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
verses.modern: The commander went to Paul and asked, "Tell me — are you a Roman citizen?" Paul said, "Yes."

verses.kjv: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
verses.modern: The commander replied, "I paid a large sum for my citizenship." Paul said, "But I was born a citizen."

verses.kjv: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
verses.modern: Those who were about to question him withdrew at once. The commander himself was alarmed when he realized Paul was a Roman citizen and he had put him in chains.

verses.kjv: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
verses.modern: The next day, wanting to find out the real reason Paul was being accused by the Jews, the commander released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole council to assemble. He brought Paul down and set him before them.

chapters.summary: Paul spoke to the crowd in Hebrew, telling them of his conversion on the road to Damascus and his commission to preach to the Gentiles. The crowd listened until he mentioned the Gentiles, then cried out for his death. The chief captain ordered him to be examined by scourging, but Paul revealed his Roman citizenship and was spared.

verses.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
verses.modern: Paul looked straight at the council and said, "Brothers, I have lived before God with a completely clear conscience to this day."

verses.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
verses.modern: The high priest Ananias commanded those standing near him to strike him on the mouth.

verses.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
verses.modern: Paul said to him, "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit there to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by ordering me to be struck."

verses.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest?
verses.modern: Those standing nearby said, "Are you insulting God's high priest?"

verses.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
verses.modern: Paul said, "Brothers, I did not know that he was the high priest. It is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"

verses.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.modern: When Paul saw that one group were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he called out in the council, "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial for my hope in the resurrection of the dead."

verses.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
verses.modern: When he said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

verses.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.modern: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, and no angel or spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge all of these.

verses.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
verses.modern: There was a great uproar. Some of the scribes who were on the Pharisees' side stood up and argued strongly: "We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?"

verses.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
verses.modern: When the argument became so violent that the commander was afraid Paul would be torn apart by them, he ordered the soldiers to go down, take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.

verses.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
verses.modern: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, "Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome."

verses.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
verses.modern: When day came, some Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath. They said they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

verses.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
verses.modern: There were more than forty of them who made this oath.

verses.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.modern: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, "We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath to eat nothing until we have killed Paul.

verses.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
verses.modern: Now then, together with the council, make a request to the commander to bring Paul down to you tomorrow, as if you were going to examine his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him before he gets here."

verses.kjv: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.modern: But the son of Paul's sister heard about this plot. He went into the barracks and told Paul.

verses.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
verses.modern: Paul called one of the centurions and said, "Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him."

verses.kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
verses.modern: The centurion took the young man to the commander and said, "The prisoner Paul called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you."

verses.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
verses.modern: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside privately, and asked, "What is it you have to tell me?"

verses.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.modern: He said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as if they intend to inquire more carefully into his case.

verses.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
verses.modern: Do not agree to it. More than forty of them are lying in ambush for him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him. They are ready now, waiting for your promise."

verses.kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
verses.modern: The commander dismissed the young man with a warning: "Tell no one that you have reported this to me."

verses.kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
verses.modern: He called two of his centurions and said, "Get two hundred soldiers ready to march to Caesarea, along with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, at nine tonight."

verses.kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
verses.modern: He also told them to provide horses for Paul to ride, so he could be brought safely to Felix the governor.

verses.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
verses.modern: He wrote a letter as follows:

verses.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
verses.modern: "Claudius Lysias, to His Excellency the governor Felix: Greetings.

verses.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
verses.modern: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them. I came with my troops and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman citizen.

verses.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
verses.modern: Wanting to know what charge they were bringing against him, I brought him before their council.

verses.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.modern: I found that he was accused about questions of their law, but no charge against him deserved death or imprisonment.

verses.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Fare thee well.
