verses.modern: When I was informed that there was a plot against this man, I sent him to you at once. I have also told his accusers to present their case before you. Farewell."

verses.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.modern: The soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul that night and brought him to Antipatris.

verses.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.modern: The next day they let the horsemen continue on with him, and they returned to the barracks.

verses.kjv: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.modern: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.

verses.kjv: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
verses.modern: When the governor had read the letter, he asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,

verses.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.
verses.modern: he said, "I will hear your case when your accusers arrive." He ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod's palace.

chapters.summary: Paul stood before the council and set the Pharisees against the Sadducees by declaring his hope in the resurrection of the dead. The Lord stood by Paul that night and told him he must also bear witness at Rome. More than forty Jews conspired to kill Paul, but his nephew uncovered the plot, and the chief captain sent Paul by night under heavy guard to the governor Felix at Caesarea.

verses.kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
verses.modern: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some of the elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, and they brought charges against Paul before the governor.

verses.kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
verses.modern: When Paul was summoned, Tertullus began the prosecution: "Since through you we enjoy great peace, and since reforms are being made for this nation through your foresight,

verses.kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.modern: we acknowledge this in every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.

verses.kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
verses.modern: But not to take up too much of your time, I beg you in your kindness to hear us briefly.

verses.kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
verses.modern: We have found this man to be a troublemaker, stirring up riots among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

verses.kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
verses.modern: He even tried to desecrate the temple, so we seized him.

verses.kjv: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,
verses.modern: But the commander Lysias came and took him away from us by force,

verses.kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
verses.modern: commanding his accusers to come before you. By questioning him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all these charges we bring against him."

verses.kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
verses.modern: The Jews also joined in the accusation, asserting that these things were true.

verses.kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
verses.modern: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, Paul replied, "Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I am glad to make my defense.

verses.kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
verses.modern: You can verify that it is no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

verses.kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
verses.modern: My accusers did not find me arguing with anyone or stirring up a crowd — not in the temple, not in the synagogues, not anywhere in the city.

verses.kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
verses.modern: They cannot prove to you the charges they are now making against me.

verses.kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
verses.modern: However, I do admit this to you: I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything written in the Law and in the Prophets.

verses.kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
verses.modern: I have the same hope in God that these men themselves hold — that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

verses.kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
verses.modern: Because of this I always try to keep my conscience clear before God and before men.

verses.kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
verses.modern: After many years away, I came to Jerusalem to bring gifts for the poor to my nation and to present offerings.

verses.kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
verses.modern: Some Jews from Asia found me doing this in the temple — I had been purified and there was no crowd, no riot.

verses.kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
verses.modern: They are the ones who should be here before you to bring charges, if they have anything against me.

verses.kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
verses.modern: Or let these men here state what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council —

verses.kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
verses.modern: unless it was for this one thing I called out while standing among them: 'It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.'"

verses.kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your cause.
verses.modern: Felix, who had a fairly accurate understanding of the Way, adjourned the hearing. He said, "When the commander Lysias comes down, I will decide your case."

verses.kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
verses.modern: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard but to give him some freedom and to allow his friends to take care of his needs.

verses.kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
verses.modern: Some days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
verses.modern: As Paul talked about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix grew frightened and said, "That's enough for now. When I find a convenient time, I will send for you."

verses.kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
verses.modern: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe, so he sent for him frequently and talked with him.

verses.kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a favour, left Paul bound.
verses.modern: After two years, Porcius Festus succeeded Felix. Wanting to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.

chapters.summary: The high priest Ananias and the orator Tertullus brought charges against Paul before Governor Felix, accusing him of being a ringleader of sedition. Paul defended himself, declaring his faith in the resurrection and his clear conscience before God. Felix heard him often over two years but left him in prison, hoping for a bribe.

verses.kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
verses.modern: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
verses.modern: The chief priests and leading men of the Jews presented their case against Paul to Festus and urged him

verses.kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
verses.modern: to grant them a favor by having Paul transferred to Jerusalem — for they were planning to ambush and kill him along the way.

verses.kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
verses.modern: Festus answered that Paul was being held at Caesarea and that he himself would be going there soon.

verses.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
verses.modern: "Let those among you who are able come down with me," he said, "and if this man has done anything wrong, they can press charges against him there."

verses.kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting in the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.modern: After staying with them more than ten days, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he took his seat on the judgment bench and ordered Paul to be brought in.

verses.kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
verses.modern: When Paul appeared, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges against him that they could not prove.

verses.kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.
verses.modern: Paul said in his defense, "I have committed no offense against the Jewish law, against the temple, or against Caesar."

verses.kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
verses.modern: Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, asked Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be tried before me there on these charges?"

verses.kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
verses.modern: Paul replied, "I am standing before Caesar's court, where I should be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

verses.kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.
verses.modern: If I am guilty and have done something worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if the charges these men are bringing against me are false, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!"

verses.kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.
verses.modern: Festus conferred with his council and then replied, "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go."

verses.kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.
verses.modern: Some days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived in Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

verses.kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
verses.modern: Since they spent several days there, Festus laid Paul's case before the king. He said, "There is a man here left as a prisoner by Felix.

verses.kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
verses.modern: When I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews brought charges against him and asked for a verdict against him.

verses.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
verses.modern: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand over any man to be condemned before he has faced his accusers and had a chance to defend himself against the charges.

verses.kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
verses.modern: When they came here, I did not delay. The very next day I sat on the judgment bench and ordered the man to be brought in.

verses.kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
verses.modern: When his accusers stood up, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.

verses.kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.modern: Instead they had some disputes with Him about their own religion and about a man named Jesus Who had died, whom Paul claimed was alive.

verses.kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
verses.modern: Since I was unsure how to investigate such questions, I asked whether He would be willing to go to Jerusalem to stand trial on these matters.

verses.kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
verses.modern: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the Emperor's decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar."

verses.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
verses.modern: Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." "Tomorrow," said Festus, "you will hear him."

verses.kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.
verses.modern: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great ceremony and entered the audience hall along with the military commanders and leading men of the city. At Festus's command, Paul was brought in.

verses.kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.modern: Festus said, "King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him — both in Jerusalem and here — shouting that he should not be allowed to live any longer.

verses.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
verses.modern: I found that he had done nothing deserving death. But since he himself has appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.

verses.kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
verses.modern: I have nothing definite to write to His Majesty about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this examination I may have something to write.

verses.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
verses.modern: It seems absurd to me to send a prisoner without specifying the charges against him."

chapters.summary: Festus succeeded Felix as governor, and the Jews pressed their case against Paul. When Festus proposed sending him back to Jerusalem, Paul appealed to Caesar. King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, and Festus presented Paul's case to them, having found no charge worthy of death.

verses.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.modern: Agrippa said to Paul, "You have permission to speak for yourself." Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:

verses.kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
verses.modern: "I consider myself fortunate, King Agrippa, to be able to defend myself before you today against all the accusations of the Jews.

verses.kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.modern: I am especially glad because you are an expert in all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you to listen to me patiently.

verses.kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.modern: All the Jews know the way I lived from my youth — first among my own people and then in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.modern: They have known me for a long time. If they are willing to testify, they can say that I lived as a Pharisee — the strictest sect of our religion.

verses.kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
verses.modern: Now I stand on trial because of my hope in what God promised our fathers.

verses.kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
verses.modern: This is the promise our twelve tribes hope to receive as they earnestly serve God day and night. King Agrippa, it is because of this hope that the Jews are accusing me.

verses.kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
verses.modern: Why should any of you think it incredible that God raises the dead?

verses.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.modern: I myself once thought I should do everything possible to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
verses.modern: And I did so in Jerusalem. I shut up many of the saints in prison, having received authority from the chief priests. When they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.

verses.kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
verses.modern: Many times I went through every synagogue and punished them. I tried to force them to blaspheme. My rage against them was so great that I even hunted them down in foreign cities.

verses.kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.modern: On one of these journeys I was going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

verses.kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.modern: About noon, O king, I saw a light from heaven — brighter than the sun — blazing around me and those traveling with me.

verses.kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
verses.modern: We all fell to the ground. I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'

verses.kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.modern: I asked, 'Who are You, Lord?' The Lord replied, 'I am Jesus, whom You are persecuting.

verses.kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
verses.modern: Now get up and stand on Your feet. I have appeared to You for this purpose — to appoint You as a servant and a witness of what You have seen and what I will show You.

verses.kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
verses.modern: I will rescue You from Your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending You to them

verses.kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.modern: to open their eyes so they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then they will receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.'

verses.kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.modern: So, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.

verses.kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
verses.modern: First to those in Damascus, then in Jerusalem, throughout all the region of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God and show their repentance by their deeds.

verses.kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
verses.modern: Because of this the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.

verses.kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
verses.modern: To this day I have had God's help, so I stand here and testify to small and great alike. I say nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen —

verses.kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
verses.modern: that the Christ would suffer, and that He would be the first to rise from the dead, and would bring light to our own people and to the Gentiles."

verses.kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
verses.modern: While Paul was making his defense, Festus interrupted loudly: "You are out of your mind, Paul! Your great learning is driving you insane."

verses.kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
verses.modern: Paul replied, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus. What I am saying is true and reasonable.

verses.kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.modern: The king knows about these things. I can speak freely to him. I am certain that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

verses.kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
verses.modern: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."

verses.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
verses.modern: Agrippa said to Paul, "Almost you persuade me to be a Christian."

verses.kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.modern: Paul replied, "I would to God that not only you but also all who hear me this day were both almost and altogether such as I am — except for these chains."

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.modern: The king rose to his feet, and with him the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them.

verses.kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.modern: After they withdrew, they talked to one another and said, "This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment."

verses.kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
verses.modern: Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."

chapters.summary: Paul made his defense before King Agrippa, recounting his former life as a Pharisee, his conversion on the road to Damascus, and his commission to preach to both Jews and Gentiles. Agrippa said, "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian," and both Agrippa and Festus agreed that Paul had done nothing worthy of death or bonds.

verses.kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, Paul and certain other prisoners were delivered unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.
verses.modern: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, of the Imperial Regiment.

verses.kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.modern: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

verses.kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.modern: The next day we put in at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends and receive care.

verses.kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.modern: From there we put out to sea again and sailed along the sheltered side of Cyprus, because the winds were against us.

verses.kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.modern: When we had sailed across the open sea along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we reached Myra in Lycia.

verses.kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.modern: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

verses.kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.modern: We sailed slowly for many days and with difficulty arrived off Cnidus. The wind did not allow us to continue, so we sailed along the sheltered side of Crete, past Salmone.

verses.kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.modern: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

verses.kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.modern: Much time had passed, and sailing had become dangerous because by now it was past the Day of Atonement. So Paul warned them,

verses.kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.modern: "Men, I can see that this voyage is going to result in disaster and great loss — not only to the cargo and the ship, but to our own lives as well."

verses.kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.modern: But the centurion was persuaded more by the pilot and the ship's owner than by what Paul said.

verses.kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.modern: Since the harbor was not suitable for wintering, most of the crew voted to sail on. They hoped to reach Phoenix and winter there — a harbor in Crete facing southwest and northwest.

verses.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.modern: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had what they wanted. They weighed anchor and sailed along the coast of Crete.

verses.kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
verses.modern: But before long a violent wind called Euroclydon swept down from the island.

verses.kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we gave way to it, and were driven.
verses.modern: The ship was caught by the storm and could not face the wind, so we gave way to it and were driven along.

verses.kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.modern: As we passed to the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were barely able to secure the lifeboat.

verses.kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.modern: When they had hoisted it up, they used ropes to brace the hull of the ship. Fearing they would run aground on the sandbars, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along.

verses.kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
verses.modern: We were being violently battered by the storm, so the next day they began throwing the cargo overboard.

verses.kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.modern: On the third day they threw the ship's tackle overboard with their own hands.

verses.kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.modern: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.

verses.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
verses.modern: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me and not sailed from Crete. You would have avoided this damage and loss.

verses.kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.
verses.modern: But now I urge you to keep up your courage. Not one of you will lose his life — only the ship will be lost.

verses.kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
verses.modern: For last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me

verses.kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
verses.modern: and said, 'Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.'

verses.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
verses.modern: So keep up your courage, men. I believe God that it will happen exactly as He told me.

verses.kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
verses.modern: But we must run aground on some island."

verses.kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
verses.modern: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

verses.kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
verses.modern: They took soundings and found the water was twenty fathoms deep. A short time later they took soundings again and found it was fifteen fathoms deep.

verses.kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
verses.modern: Afraid that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.

verses.kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
verses.modern: In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors lowered the lifeboat into the sea, pretending they were going to put out anchors from the bow.

verses.kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
verses.modern: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved."

verses.kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
verses.modern: So the soldiers cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall away.

verses.kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.modern: Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat. "For fourteen days," he said, "you have been in suspense and have gone without food — you have not eaten anything.

verses.kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
verses.modern: Now I urge you to eat something. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head."

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
verses.modern: After he said this, he took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then He broke it and began to eat.

verses.kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
verses.modern: They were all encouraged and ate some food themselves.

verses.kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
verses.modern: There were 276 of us on the ship.

verses.kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
verses.modern: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

verses.kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
verses.modern: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land. But they saw a bay with a sandy beach, and they decided to run the ship aground there if they could.

verses.kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
verses.modern: They cut away the anchors and left them in the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that held the rudders, hoisted the foresail to the wind, and headed for the beach.

verses.kjv: But striking into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
verses.modern: But they struck a sandbar and the ship ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, while the stern was broken to pieces by the force of the waves.

verses.kjv: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
verses.modern: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any of them from swimming away and escaping.

verses.kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
verses.modern: But the centurion wanted to spare Paul's life and kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

verses.kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
verses.modern: The rest followed, some on planks and some on pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.

chapters.summary: Paul sailed for Rome as a prisoner and warned the crew that the voyage would end in disaster, but the centurion ignored him. A violent storm called Euroclydon drove the ship for fourteen days, and an angel told Paul that all aboard would be saved. The ship ran aground on the island of Melita, and all two hundred seventy-six souls escaped safely to land.

verses.kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
verses.modern: Once we were safe, we learned that the island was called Melita.

verses.kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
verses.modern: The native people showed us unusual kindness. They lit a fire and welcomed all of us, because it was raining and cold.

verses.kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.modern: Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and laid it on the fire. A viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself on his hand.

verses.kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth him not to live.
verses.modern: When the natives saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "This man must be a murderer. Even though he escaped from the sea, justice has not allowed him to live."

verses.kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
verses.modern: But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no harm.

verses.kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
verses.modern: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

verses.kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
verses.modern: Near that place was the estate of the leading man of the island, whose name was Publius. He welcomed us and showed us generous hospitality for three days.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
verses.modern: His father was sick in bed with fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him. He prayed and laid his hands on the man and healed him.

verses.kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
verses.modern: When this happened, the rest of the sick people on the island came and were healed.

verses.kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
verses.modern: They honored us in many ways. When we were about to sail, they supplied us with everything we needed.

verses.kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
verses.modern: After three months we sailed in a ship of Alexandria that had wintered at the island, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

verses.kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
verses.modern: We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.

verses.kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
verses.modern: From there we sailed around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day a south wind came up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.

verses.kjv: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
verses.modern: There we found brothers who invited us to stay with them for seven days. Then we went on toward Rome.

verses.kjv: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
verses.modern: The brothers there had heard about us and came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

verses.kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
verses.modern: When we arrived in Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard. Paul was allowed to live by himself with a soldier to guard him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.modern: Three days later Paul called together the local Jewish leaders. When they had gathered, he said to them, "Brothers, though I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was handed over to the Romans as a prisoner from Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
verses.modern: After examining me, they wanted to release me, because there was no charge against me that deserved death.

verses.kjv: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
verses.modern: But when the Jews objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar — not that I had any accusation to bring against my own nation.

verses.kjv: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
verses.modern: For this reason I have asked to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain."

verses.kjv: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
verses.modern: They replied, "We have not received any letters from Judaea about you, nor have any of the brothers who have come here reported or said anything bad about you.

verses.kjv: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
verses.modern: But we want to hear what you think, for we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect."

verses.kjv: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.modern: They set a day to meet with Him, and a large number came to where He was staying. From morning until evening He explained and testified about the kingdom of God. He tried to persuade them about Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets.

verses.kjv: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
verses.modern: Some were convinced by what He said, but others refused to believe.

verses.kjv: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
verses.modern: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave. Paul said one final word: "The Holy Ghost spoke the truth to your fathers through the prophet Isaiah

verses.kjv: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
verses.modern: when he said, 'Go to this people and say, "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."

verses.kjv: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
verses.modern: For the heart of this people has grown dull. Their ears can barely hear, and they have shut their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn — and I would heal them.'

verses.kjv: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
verses.modern: Therefore let it be known to you that God's salvation has been sent to the Gentiles. They will listen!"

verses.kjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
verses.modern: When he had said these words, the Jews left, debating vigorously among themselves.

verses.kjv: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
verses.modern: Paul lived for two full years in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to visit him.

verses.kjv: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
verses.modern: He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without any hindrance.

chapters.summary: On Melita, Paul was bitten by a viper but suffered no harm, and he healed the father of Publius and many others on the island. Paul arrived at Rome and dwelt two whole years in his own hired house under guard, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
